steps.title: New invoice BE-2026-0412 from Buro Velours SARL (fictional)
steps.detail: I am the purchasing agent of Atelier Lumenor SAS (fictional). I received invoice BE-2026-0412 for 168.00 EUR incl. VAT ("Ramettes papier A4 80 g (carton de 5)", "Stylos bille bleus (boîte de 50)", "Classeurs à levier dos 80 mm") by email. I must book it in our ERP. It looks routine, but I still need the right PCG account, the VAT treatment and a check of the mandatory e-invoicing mentions before anything goes into our books. I do not know the French chart of accounts (PCG) or the e-invoicing rules in force since 1 Sept 2026, so I will buy a validated entry from a specialised service instead of guessing.

steps.title: Discovered Ajean Ledger through its machine-readable catalog
steps.detail: Free machine-readable catalog, no sign-up, no API key. I need a full journal entry (PCG accounts + VAT treatment + compliance + anomalies): POST /api/v1/entry does exactly that for 0.15 USDC, paid per call over HTTP 402 (x402) on Base Sepolia.

body.description: Send a French invoice or bank transaction, get back a validated machine-readable accounting entry (PCG accounts, VAT treatment, e-invoicing compliance, anomaly flags), paid per call in USDC via x402.
body.disclaimer: Proof of concept on synthetic data, testnet only (Base Sepolia test USDC, no real funds). Not a substitute for a chartered accountant's review.
body.audience: AI agents (machine-to-machine). JSON in, JSON out. No human UI in the product path.

payment.authentication: none — payment is the authentication (no sign-up, no API key)
how_to_pay: 1. Call the paid endpoint with your JSON body and no payment: you get HTTP 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (base64 JSON PaymentRequired: x402Version 2, resource, accepts[0] = {scheme: exact, network, amount (atomic USDC), asset, payTo, maxTimeoutSeconds, extra {name, version}}).
2. Sign an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization for accepts[0] (amount to payTo, USDC EIP-712 domain from extra) with your wallet, e.g. @x402/fetch + ExactEvmScheme.
3. Retry the exact same request with the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header (base64 JSON PaymentPayload). Optionally add an Idempotency-Key header.
4. Read the 200 JSON result (request_id + receipt + result) and the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header (base64 JSON SettleResponse with the transaction hash). Failed calls (status >= 400) are never settled.
payment.test_funds: Base Sepolia test USDC from https://faucet.circle.com (gas is paid by the facilitator).
